title: Saying, thinking, naming
goal: Link a quote or a thought to another verb with diýip, say what you think with öýtmek, and name things.

intro.text: *Diýip*, literally **saying**, links a quote to another verb: *“Nirede?” diýip sorady*. It also brings in a thought: *Ýagyş ýagar diýip pikir etdim*, I thought it would rain. With *öýtmek* (to think, to suppose) the thought comes straight before it: *Ol geler öýdýärin*.

vocab.en: saying (after a quote or a thought); so that
to think, to suppose (öýdýärin: I think)
to name, to give a name (to)

exercises.question: *“Gijä galdym” diýip ylgady.* What happened?
options: He said he was late and ran off.
Someone shouted at him, so he ran.

why.1: The words in the quote are his own: *Gijä galdym*, I'm late.
why.2: *Ylgady* is what he did: he ran. What he said was *Gijä galdym*.

exercises.explain: *diýip* (saying) links his words to what he did: *ylgady*, he ran.

reject.why: Two verbs of saying in a row: link the quote to *sorady* with the converb, *diýip*.

exercises.explain: Quote + *diýip* + the verb of saying: *diýip sorady*.

reject.why: Inside the quote, keep your own words: *Gelmerin*, I won't come.

exercises.explain: The quote, then *diýip aýtdym*, I told (him) saying. The person told takes the dative: *oňa*.

accept: I thought it was going to rain
I thought that it would rain
I thought that it was going to rain

exercises.question: How do you say **I think he's right**?

why.2: *Aýtdy* is past: **I think he said it right**.

exercises.explain: The thought as it would be said, *Ol dogry aýdýar*, then *öýdýärin*, I think.

exercises.label: *öýtmek* (to think, to suppose), present: I think, you think…
exercises.explain: The *t* of *öýt-* softens to *d* before *-ýär*, as in *gidýär*: *öýdýärin*.

accept: Olar ogluna Batyr diýip at dakdylar.
exercises.explain: The name, then *diýip at dakmak*: to give a name, saying “Batyr”. The child takes the dative: *ogluna*.

exercises.text: Biz pişige Gara diýip at dakdyk.

exercises.explain: Before another verb of saying, *jogap berdi*, the quote takes *diýip*.

accept: Men ol geler diýip pikir etdim.

reject.why: *Pikir edýärin* is **I think**, now. **I thought**: *pikir etdim*.

exercises.explain: The thought as it was thought, *Ol geler*, then *diýip pikir etdim*, or just *öýtdüm*.

accept: They used to call him Kemine

exercises.question: *Merdan “Men gelerin” diýdi.* Who will come?
options: the person he is talking to

why.1: Inside the quote, *men* is the speaker: Merdan.
why.2: *Men* in his quote is Merdan himself.

exercises.explain: A quote keeps the speaker's own words: *Men gelerin*, I'll come, said by Merdan.
